16 A wooden cylinder floats partially submerged in a bath of water. A force F is applied to the
cylinder until it is just fully submerged.
wooden cylinder
water
F
Which statement is not correct?
A
Some of the water gains gravitational potential energy.
B
The cylinder loses gravitational potential energy.
C
Work is done by force F on the cylinder.
D
Work is done by the upthrust on the cylinder.

hints: Notice the direction of motion of the cylinder when $F$ pushes it from partly submerged to just fully submerged.
Compare the upward direction of upthrust with the downward displacement to decide the sign of $W = Fs\cos\theta$.
Check what happens to the displaced water level while the cylinder moves down to see the change in water $mgh$.
walkthrough: Identify the displacements: the cylinder moves downward into the water, while displaced water is forced outward and the free surface rises.
State the work rule: work done by a force is $W = Fs\cos\theta$, positive if force and displacement are in the same direction and negative if opposite.
Apply to $F$: $F$ is downward and displacement is downward, so $\theta = 0$ and positive work is done by $F$ on the cylinder.
Apply to weight and position: downward motion lowers the cylinder so it loses gravitational potential energy, while raised water gains gravitational potential energy.

Apply to upthrust: upthrust on the cylinder is upward but displacement is downward, so $\theta = 180^{\circ}$ and the work done by upthrust is negative, not positive work done on the cylinder. This is option D.

A.explanation: This statement is correct physics: pushing the cylinder down displaces water upward and raises the water level, so some water gains $mgh$.

B.explanation: This statement is correct physics: the centre of mass of the cylinder moves down, so its gravitational potential energy decreases.

C.explanation: This statement is correct physics: force $F$ acts downward and the cylinder moves downward, so $W = Fd$ is positive.

D.explanation: This statement is not correct as positive work: upthrust acts upward while displacement is downward, so upthrust does negative work, not positive work on the cylinder.
